business: GradTrail, a free, open-source, self-hosted job-search and application workspace
why_not: I already check several boards and career pages, and running a database plus provider keys sounds like more setup than I want to take on while job hunting. I might try it if I could see it working on my laptop without spending an evening configuring it.

The free tracker sounds useful, but I need confidence that dates and deadlines are accurate before I spend time applying. Running a server and setting up provider keys is too much friction for me to try another job tool right now.

Self-hosting sounds like it could give me more control, but the pitch does not explain what resume or application data is stored or what I need to configure. I would keep using my current tools until I can see a clear privacy explanation and try it without putting my real details in.

I like that it can use my projects and lets me review AI drafts, but I cannot tell how it prevents made-up claims or how much of setup and usage will cost me. Since I can already track applications in a spreadsheet, I would wait for a real demo before installing another tool.
why_yes: I would try it because I like keeping application data under my control, and the software itself is free. I would check the project-based AI draft carefully and stop if setup or provider costs became a hassle.
